text.card: Sow a house count rightward; follow the forced relay to collect eight in Ruma.
text.read_counts: Read all five counts and the relay pointer; choose an offered sow with that house count and landing condition.
text.empty_hands: Put down what you hold before using the sowing board.
text.rules: Classic fixed start: houses 1 to 4 each show two units; Ruma R starts empty. One action sows the chosen nonempty house: remove its entire count and add one to each successive pit to the right, including Ruma, wrapping from Ruma to house 1. Never sow from Ruma. When the last unit lands in Ruma, choose any nonempty house. Otherwise, if its landing house was already occupied, the next action must sow that house. Landing in a previously empty house loses. All eight in Ruma is the goal. Each action is one sow, not an automatic chain.
text.display: Each gold mounted cap represents one count unit. The purple pointer beside blue C means choice, above a numbered house means that house is forced, and beside red X means loss. The rightward and wrap arrows show direction. Houses have maximum counts 4,3,3,4 and Ruma 8 in this classic setup. Inspect house1, house2, house3, house4, ruma and relay for exact values; relay 0=choice,1 to 4=forced house,5=loss.
text.solution: One complete solution uses houses 3,4,2,3,4,1,4,2,3,4. These are ten separate sow actions, including mandatory relays, or six completed chains in the paper terminology. The board stores no move count or solution solver.
text.loss_restart: Starting with house 1 forces house 3; sowing house 3 then loses by landing in a previously empty house. Explicit restart restores two in each house, empty Ruma and choice. Restart is a trainer control for a new attempt, not continuing a lost game. It is available from any state.
text.limits: This board supports the classic 2222|0 start and its reachable histories. It is not arbitrary setup or generalized Mancala. Some natural sows in unreachable externally authored histories have no offered form. The twenty-two integral potential count caps are a symbolic display, not eight portable physical beans. No per-bean trajectory, custody, material transfer, score, turn, history or automatic relay is claimed.
text.source: Rules follow Campbell and Chavey, Tchuka Ruma Solitaire, The UMAP Journal 16(4), 1995, pages 343 to 345. Original mounted drawing; no source artwork copied and no definite cultural-origin attribution.
